THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the Judgment and Award dated 11.05.2016 passed in MVC.No.856/2010 by the Additional District and NC: 2024:KHC:32874 Sessions Judge and Additional MACT, Udupi (sitting at Kundapura), Kundapura (in short, 'the Tribunal').

Rakshith Mogaveera vs Mr. Sathish on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158973303/
2 2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 13.08.2010 at about 5.00 p.m., while the petitioner was proceeding in the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-20/S-1363 as pillion rider, on Mandarthi-Barkur main road,
Heggunje village, Udupi Taluk, an Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-20/A-4776 hit against the motorcycle.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
After taking treatment at Government hospital and Chinmayi hospital, Kundapura, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.6,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the insurance companies of both motorcycle and Auto Rickshaw.

The Tribunal, after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties by the impugned judgment allowed the claim petition, granting compensation of Rs.95,185/-
NC: 2024:KHC:32874 directed the owner and driver of the Auto Rickshaw to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner is before this Court on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Ms. Swati G. Hegde, learned counsel for Sri H.Pavanachandra Shetty,
learned counsel for the petitioner, Shri.O.Mahesh, learned counsel for respondent No.3 and Smt.Mamatha S. Shankar, learned counsel for respondent No.6.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner being a 19 years old student and also doing agriculture has suffered fracture of both bones and he was under hospitalization for 10 days.
The medical evidence placed through PW.2-Dr.Dinesh Kumar Shetty, explaining whole body disability at 10%.

The Tribunal did not consider loss of future income and has awarded lesser compensation towards loss of income during laid NC: 2024:KHC:32874 up and incidental expenses and sought for enhancement.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance companies have contended that the driver of Auto Rickshaw was the tortfeasor, hence the owner and driver of the Auto Rickshaw have to pay the compensation as on the date of accident policy was not in force and the owner, rider and insurer of motorcycle are the formal parties.
The Tribunal has rightly considered non-availability of the insurance coverage and directed the driver and owner of Auto Rickshaw to pay the compensation and has supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.

8. The evidence placed on record clearly points out that involvement of Auto Rickshaw and motorcycle NC: 2024:KHC:32874 in an accident, the petitioner being pillion rider of the motor cycle hit by Auto Rickshaw.
Admittedly there is no insurance cover for Auto Rickshaw on the date of accident as it was lapsed as indicated in Ex.R4- insurance policy.
The tortfeasor is the driver of Auto Rickshaw and there is no aspect of contributory negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle.

Rakshith Mogaveera vs Mr. Sathish on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158973303/
3
Hence, in the absence of policy coverage, the driver and owner of Auto Rickshaw have to pay the compensation and the Tribunal has rightly recorded its finding.
9. As regarding quantum of compensation is concerned, the medical evidence shows that the petitioner has suffered fracture of both bones of right leg and he was under hospitalization for 10 days.
PW.2-Dr.Dineshkumar Shetty has assessed limb disability at 10%.
Having regard to the age of the petitioner as 19 years and a student, fracture of both bones of right leg certainly affect his future at 5%.
In NC: 2024:KHC:32874 the year 2005, a person with no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.5,500/- per month.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.5,500/- per month and multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.

Then loss of future income due to disability comes to Rs.5,500/-x12x18x5%=59,400/-.
10.
The Tribunal has assessed Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.34,185/- towards medical evidence which required to be reimbursed and same is kept intact.
The petitioner was laid up for minimum 3 months and for loss of income due to laid up at Rs.16,500/- (Rs.5,500/- x 3 months) is assessed.
Towards loss of amenities and discomfort is assessed at Rs.25,000/- and towards attendant, food and nourishment and traveling expenses is assessed at Rs.8,000/-.

Then total compensation comes to Rs.1,73,085/- as against Rs.95,185/-, thereby enhanced compensation of Rs.77,900/-, rounded off to Rs.78,000/-, which is the just compensation that NC:
2024:KHC:32874 petitioner is entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case.

Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part;
ii) Impugned judgment and award is modified.
iii) Petitioner would be entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.78,000/- along with interest of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 i.e. driver and owner of Auto Rickshaw are liable to pay compensation with interest within 8 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE MKM Rakshith Mogaveera vs Mr. Sathish on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158973303/
